sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: No supplied candidate is semantically verified: hasComponent is explicitly ship-owned and its range is shipComponent, while hasRudderProtectionArrangement links a ship to a rudderProtectionArrangement but does not connect that arrangement to an iceKnife. The required owner-compatible arrangement-to-iceKnife path is absent.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the applicability alternatives: do not require iceKnifePracticable=true for every IA/IA Super case while also offering equivalent means. Encode explicit branches selected by the supplied practicability evidence: when iceKnifePracticable=true, require a rudder protection arrangement containing an iceKnife with extendsBelowLowerIceWaterline=true; when it is false, require the equivalentRudderProtectionMeans alternative and do not require the ice-knife extension. Preserve IA/IA Super applicability, ship ownership, the LIWL input, and the canonical datatypes.

The applicability branching is now correctly tied to iceKnifePracticable, but the practicable branch still does not faithfully encode an arrangement containing an ice knife: it requires the same arrangement node to be both rudderProtectionArrangement and iceKnife via conjunctive sh:class constraints. Encode the ice knife as the required linked component of the rudder-protection arrangement using the supplied owner-compatible relationship/path, and constrain that iceKnife node with extendsBelowLowerIceWaterline=true. Preserve the false branch, IA/IA Super applicability, ship-owned inputs, LIWL input, and canonical datatypes; do not add a convenience applicability flag or invent a vocabulary term.

The practicable branch still does not link the required ice knife to the rudder-protection arrangement: separate ship-level hasRudderProtectionArrangement and hasComponent constraints can be satisfied by unrelated nodes. Add or locate a canonical owner-compatible relationship/path that connects the arrangement to its iceKnife component, then constrain that linked iceKnife with extendsBelowLowerIceWaterline=true. Do not place hasComponent on the arrangement because its declared domain is ship, and do not make one node conjunctively both rudderProtectionArrangement and iceKnife. Preserve the existing explicit true/false applicability branches, IA/IA Super applicability, ship-owned inputs, and canonical datatypes.
